summary: Creates the multidisciplinary team and product practices needed to research, map, design, build, test, release and continuously improve student-facing digital capabilities.
detailSummary:
The Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability will establish a sustained multidisciplinary team around the continued evolution of the Student Experience Hub. The team will combine software engineering, product and experience design, service design, user research, business analysis, quality engineering and agile delivery, drawing on specialist architecture, data, integration, security, accessibility, change and service-management expertise through clear working interfaces.

The first year now carries two substantial delivery demands in parallel. The team must protect the rapid King’s Edge replatform and richer functionality committed through 4.1.4, while also building the common Hub shell and integrating timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s for a September 2027 production release under 4.1.2. These are not separate products or teams: they are two protected delivery lanes within one shared product capability, using the same architecture, standards, research, assurance and release practices.

The deliverable focuses on who delivers and how they work. It will establish one transparent product pipeline, explicit capacity allocation and trade-off decisions, disciplined discovery and prioritisation, continuous student and staff involvement, journey mapping and service blueprinting, proportionate prototyping, engineering and quality practices, embedded assurance, controlled release, evaluation and a clear route into supported operation or clean closure.

The Student Experience Hub product, its journey and experience outputs, app architecture, platform foundations and operating costs are owned through 4.1.2. The team established here provides the methods and capacity needed to deliver those outputs while also supporting the King’s Edge product demand under 4.1.4.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary team or consistent product practices for turning emerging student-experience needs into working and sustainable digital capabilities.

Requirements are often addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products. Demand can be difficult to prioritise, cross-service journeys may not be understood before solutions are selected, users may be involved too late, and promising prototypes can struggle to move through quality, assurance, release and support.

The first-year programme now also creates a concrete capacity challenge. King’s needs to deliver a substantial protected King’s Edge roadmap while simultaneously establishing a broader Student Experience Hub, integrating three additional priority sources and preparing the combined service for production in September 2027. A small undifferentiated development pod would create an avoidable choice between breadth and depth, or carry unacceptable delivery and quality risk.
caseForChange.opportunity:
A sustained multidisciplinary team with clear product practices can give King’s a faster and more disciplined route from need to supported change.

One transparent pipeline can connect prioritisation, user research, service design, journey mapping, business analysis, prototyping, engineering, quality, assurance, release and evaluation. Within that pipeline, protected delivery capacity can support both deep domain development and common platform and integration work without creating separate teams or technical estates.

Students and service owners can shape decisions while solutions remain adaptable, and specialist Digital and IT functions can be involved throughout rather than acting only as late-stage gates. The same team and practices can therefore deliver the protected King’s Edge roadmap under 4.1.4, build and harden the September 2027 Hub release under 4.1.2 and then scale across wider student journeys.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is generating an immediate pipeline of substantial product requirements at exactly the point when the Student Experience Hub is being accelerated into a production student front door for September 2027.

That combination changes the first-year capacity requirement. Two product engineers may be sufficient for a tightly bounded replatforming stream, but they do not provide credible resilience for concurrent Edge feature development, common-app work, three additional integrations, iterative student prototypes, production hardening and launch support. Quality engineering and integration capacity also need to be present before the release candidate, rather than added only after launch.

Establishing the fuller team from the start allows the first year to prove both the product capability and the shared Hub proposition without sacrificing the agreed depth of King’s Edge delivery.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has an enduring multidisciplinary digital product team with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for user research, journey mapping, service design, business analysis, prototyping, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

The team can sustain more than one protected delivery lane within a single coherent product capability. During the first year it can deliver the deep King’s Edge roadmap and the horizontal Student Experience Hub in parallel, while making capacity constraints and trade-offs explicit rather than allowing one stream to displace the other silently.

Emerging needs are explored with students and service owners before substantial commitment. Cross-service journeys and constraints are made visible, work moves predictably from evidence and prototype into controlled live use, supported operation or clean closure, and live-service evidence directly informs what the team does next.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent research, service-design, delivery and assurance practices make student needs, priorities, progress, trade-offs and release decisions clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, protected delivery commitments are visible, delivery cycles use consistent evidence and standards, and capacity and release decisions can be explained and reviewed.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while the team and its professional capability remain available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first harden-or-close cycle, increasing as the team becomes recurrent
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the multidisciplinary team has an approved route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the core multidisciplinary team from September through November 2026. Mobilise sufficient engineering, integration and quality capacity to protect the King’s Edge roadmap while building the September 2027 Hub release, and confirm how service design, user research and business analysis will be provided alongside the funded core team.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one product operating model with transparent intake, prioritisation and explicit capacity allocation across the protected King’s Edge and Hub delivery lanes, alongside discovery, user research, service design, prototyping, engineering, quality, assurance and release practices.

steps.title: Prove concurrent delivery through King’s Edge and the first Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that one multidisciplinary capability can deliver the protected King’s Edge roadmap and the horizontal Student Experience Hub in parallel. Use repeated discovery, build, integration, quality, assurance, beta, hardening and live-release cycles to refine team roles, capacity allocation and specialist handoffs.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make the team’s operating practices routine across the live Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices across the wider app roadmap
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, apply the established operating model across a growing portfolio of student journeys. Increase throughput and support concurrent work while preserving continuous user involvement, disciplined prioritisation, quality, embedded assurance, learning and sustainable ownership.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: From November 2028 to June 2029, establish the multidisciplinary team, its recurrent staffing, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT services as an enduring institutional capability.
